title: Reading Drill — Testing sign visibility from buses — Reviewing the evidence
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Testing sign visibility from buses — Reviewing the evidence
passages.body:
**A** The transit accessibility panel in Brackenton received an old report about street signs passing too quickly for passengers to read. The report compared the proportion of signs recognised, but some entries had been collected under different conditions. To check the report, reviewers returned to the timed rides rather than treating the published figures as a complete record.

**B** The review covered eight weeks. In the first part of that period, the original records did not consistently include seats on the window side. In the later part, the recording sheet included a separate field for it. The reviewers kept readings from both periods, but marked which items were missing rather than guessing what had happened.

**C** The conclusion listed larger lettering as a possible later response. It recommended collecting another set of readings before deciding whether to use it. The new data would be published with the method, so another group could work out whether its own measurements were comparable.
